thread:
maya: Morning — FYI the overnight run flagged a sharp entropy/kl spike for the "LegalDocs" cohort on redwood-v2-q4.3, multiple suites failed. not noise? :warning:
eval-bot: [ALERT] nightly-eval: 2026-03-19T07:00Z. model=redwood-v2-q4.3; failed_suites=[legal_extraction, instruction_following, extractive_answers]; fail_rates=[0.18, 0.12, 0.22]; delta_fail=[+0.12, +0.08, +0.14]; avg_kl=1.9 -> baseline 0.42; avg_entropy=5.8 -> baseline 3.1
simon: on it. first pass: rerun the three failing suites against fp16 baseline and q4 variant on the same infra. posting rerun command now.

rachel: quick question — did this only happen on q4 quantized variants? last week's rolling deploy touched a new kernel set on infer-runtime so want to know if it's quantization-only or runtime-related.
eval-bot: rerun-requested: ids -> rerun-31625-01 (q4), rerun-31625-02 (fp16).
simon: running `python eval/run.py --model redwood-v2-q4.3 --suite legal_extraction,instruction_following,extractive_answers --cohort LegalDocs --run-id rerun-31625-01 --workers 16` and the same with `--model redwood-v2-fp16 --run-id rerun-31625-02`. ETA ~45m.
deb: triage checklist suggestion: 1) rerun q4 vs fp16 (simon). 2) sample generations + exact diffs on tokenization & prefix lengths (jonah). 3) check kv-cache alignment and batch shapes on the infer nodes (rachel/eng-runtime). 4) sanity-check eval harness for changes in scoring scripts (maya).
jonah: pasting a couple of the worst samples I pulled from the initial run:```
PROMPT: Extract clause about indemnification from contract snippet.
GOLD: "Section 7.2: Each party shall indemnify..."
MODEL (q4.3): "No indemnity exists in this agreement. The parties agree to hold harmless and not be liable. See clause 2."
NOTES: hallucinated negation + dropped section reference.```
maya: yikes — that looks like a direct hallucination/contradiction, not just formatting. that increases severity in my book. marking as P2 (regression impacting correctness).
rachel: I'm going to check infer-runtime logs for the q4 kernel change and also validate whether the kernel rollout toggled on the west-1 pool last night. if kernel mismatch -> escalate to eng-runtime.
simon: quick interim plan: (A) rerun and compare real-time logits / topk distributions for the failing prompts (B) run eval with `--deterministic` to see if variance is large (C) run tensor-level `kl_div` diff between runs. I'll upload diffs to the rerun artifact bucket when done.
deb: should we rollback the q4 rollout on west-1 preemptively? might be noisy but reduces customer risk if this is deployment-related.
maya: don't rollback yet — wait for the fp16 vs q4 comparison. if fp16 is good and q4 is bad, then consider rollback. owner: simon primary, rachel secondary. tagging @eng-runtime if kernel mismatch confirmed.
simon: noted. I'll update thread + create EVAL ticket: EVAL-1247 with findings + attach failing samples.
jonah: I'll prepare a short promptset to stress extractive QA and run it against both run-ids; also check tokenizer edgecases around legal formatting (bullets, section numbers).
maya: timeline: expect first artifacts in ~1hr, full triage summary by EOD. if severity worsens to P1 (customer visible), we'll page.
eval-bot: status update: rerun-31625-01 (q4) complete. rerun-31625-02 (fp16) running. artifacts: s3://eval-artifacts/31625/rerun-31625-01/*
simon: preliminary diff: q4 shows elevated avg_kl on LegalDocs subset (1.7 vs 0.45 fp16 baseline from previous week). attaching short CSV to ticket.
maya: thanks — everyone please add any odd samples to EVAL-1247. I'll sync with product on potential downstream customer impact. closing for now until rerun completes.
